claims.statement: EU policy promotes selective demolition and pre-demolition audits, but the Commission describes its protocol and audit guidance as non-binding and Polish law does not itself create a general paid-audit mandate.

Since 1 January 2025 Polish producers of construction and demolition waste must ensure separation of specified fractions, may contract the duty in writing to an authorized entity, and retain joint liability under the cited amendment.

The new Construction Products Regulation covers used products and future harmonized specifications, while products directly reused in a construction work are not considered placed on the market again; status and conformity therefore depend on the route and product class.

JRC evidence places pre-demolition audit cost around EUR 3000-5000 for demolition projects up to EUR 300000 and says effectiveness and economic benefit remain uncertain, especially for small projects.
Concular already combines pre-deconstruction audits, AI-assisted inventory, marketplace distribution, logistics, and optional insured or warranted installation, closely matching the proposed offer.

Marketplace evidence is mixed: Greyn offers free listing and charges only on sale, while RAEDIFICARE advertises no sales commission and reported EUR 125000 across 175 orders in 2024, about EUR 714 per order.

contrary_evidence: Pre-demolition audit guidance is non-binding and JRC found no direct effectiveness evidence for economic modelling.
JRC says small projects can face disproportionate administrative burden and EEA notes low-cost virgin inputs, weak standards, and quality doubts.
Concular already provides the integrated audit, inventory, marketplace, logistics, and insurance stack.
Greyn's free listing and RAEDIFICARE's no-commission model constrain marketplace take rates; RAEDIFICARE's reported average order value is low.
Used components can cross construction-product conformity and waste-law boundaries, and waste-market intermediaries enter BDO registration and recordkeeping scope.
A planned EU digital pre-demolition data platform could expand demand while commoditizing inventory data and crowding out a standalone exchange.

economics.acquisition_route: Sell one paid portfolio-screening pilot to one commercial property owner or demolition contractor, review its forward pipeline, and advance only substantial sites whose conservative recoverable-value estimate exceeds audit, removal, specialist, and coordination cost.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The prior arithmetic of 250 projects at 18000 PLN blended revenue, 25% EBITDA, and a 5x multiple remains only a sensitivity reference and is not evidence for this redesign. A founder-net-worth path now depends on repeat paid portfolio retainers, a sufficient gate-passing site rate, delegated delivery, and proven contribution margins; none is established, and meaningful throughput would still require an operating team without assuming founder dilution or double-counting distributions.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly if all field work, testing, removal, transport, storage, and waste handling are delegated to insured specialists.
economics.gross_margin_basis: The retainer is intended to fund lightweight pipeline triage, while specialist-heavy audits occur only after a site clears the value-to-delivery-cost hurdle. The prior 50-65% full-audit gross-margin target remains an unvalidated hypothesis after contracted field survey and specialist review; destructive sampling, engineering review, hazardous-material work, removal, storage, transport, and warranty stay outside the fee or are passed through.
economics.payback: Revised payback cannot be estimated from reviewed evidence because retainer price, screening cost, gate pass rate, and completed-sale volume are unknown. The prior reference of roughly ten 12500 PLN projects at 60% contribution to recover 75000 PLN setup cash is not transferred to this redesigned model as a forecast.
economics.pricing: Test a negotiated paid recurring screening retainer, whose price is unvalidated; retain the 12000-25000 PLN starting test for a scoped full audit and coordination plan only on a gate-passing site, plus 3-8% only for completed high-value product sales. Low-value lots remain outside commission-dependent delivery.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Retention is tied to a portfolio owner's or demolition contractor's recurring forward pipeline and willingness to keep paying for screening; both the retainer and repeat volume remain unvalidated, while individual salvage buyers and lots remain irregular.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A proprietary paired record of screened site characteristics, gate decisions, buyer acceptance criteria, removal yields, project timing, completed outcomes, and lawful fallback routes improves portfolio triage and quoting
fingerprint.customer: Polish commercial property portfolio owners and demolition contractors with recurring forward pipelines of substantial renovation or demolition projects and pre-sellable non-structural components
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner with a small number of demolition contractors, property managers, architects, and licensed waste operators rather than building an open consumer marketplace
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Recurring portfolio pipeline screening, followed by a paid pre-demolition audit and coordination plan only for sites that clear a conservative recoverable-value-to-delivery-cost hurdle; the first wedge covers pre-sellable non-structural components, success fees apply only to completed product sales, and regulated waste handling remains with one licensed operator of record
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A portfolio owner or demolition contractor pays a recurring pipeline-screening retainer, then a per-site audit and coordination fee only after the site clears the value-to-delivery-cost hurdle; a separately disclosed success fee is earned only on a completed product sale
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An owner or demolition contractor reviews a forward renovation or demolition pipeline and must decide which sites merit specialist reuse work before procurement, deinstallation, or waste classification closes the option

founder_fit: Portfolio screening, structured inventories, hurdle calibration, and evidence reconciliation fit the founder's data and AI skills.
A small set of recurring portfolio relationships is less socially intensive than repeated one-off owner acquisition or a consumer marketplace.
The non-structural wedge and licensed-operator-of-record model can delegate field surveys, hazardous-material work, removal, storage, transport, and regulated waste handling.
The pilot can remain asset-light within the existing 75000 PLN capital assumption, but recurring-retainer demand and screening workload are unvalidated.
Gate-passing sites still create deadline-sensitive coordination and exception handling, and meaningful scale would require a full-time operating team.

redesign.economic_effect: Shifts revenue from a one-off full audit on every acquired site to a recurring portfolio-screening fee plus full-audit revenue only for sites that clear a conservative recoverable-value-to-delivery-cost hurdle. This is intended to reduce wasted specialist delivery and dependence on percentage commissions, while narrowing early execution to non-structural lots and assigning regulated waste handling to one licensed operator of record; retainer demand, hurdle accuracy, buyer liquidity, legal scope, and margins remain unvalidated.

risks: Hazardous-material exposure and incomplete building records
BDO noncompliance if waste brokerage or possession is mishandled
Demolition delay, removal damage, storage, and transport overruns
Low lot value relative to audit and deconstruction cost
Powerful full-stack incumbents and free marketplace substitutes
Operational intensity incompatible with part-time scale
Portfolio owners or demolition contractors reject a paid recurring screening retainer
Insufficient early site data makes the value-to-delivery-cost gate unreliable
The initial non-structural component classes still lack enough buyer liquidity for economical removal
The operator-of-record contract does not eliminate the service's own lot-specific BDO, product-status, or liability duties

structure.commercial_archetype: Recurring portfolio pipeline-screening retainer with gated reuse audits and transaction coordination
structure.control_point: The recurring portfolio review and owner-authorised gate before specialist audit spend, deinstallation, or waste classification closes reuse options
structure.critical_dependency: Enough early site data to apply the value-to-delivery-cost hurdle, clear title and product status for each non-structural lot, safe removal evidence, and one licensed operator of record whenever material is waste

thesis: Sell a recurring pipeline-screening service to a Polish commercial property portfolio owner or demolition contractor, then advance only substantial sites whose conservative recoverable-value estimate exceeds audit, removal, specialist, and coordination cost. For the initial wedge, coordinate only pre-sellable non-structural components; place any regulated waste handling under one licensed operator of record and do not take inventory. The customer pays for continuing portfolio triage and for a full audit only after the site clears the hurdle, with a separately disclosed success fee limited to completed product sales. This redesign reduces exposure to uneconomic audits and thin general-marketplace commissions, but recurring-retainer demand, hurdle accuracy, Polish buyer liquidity, legal scope, and delivery margins remain unvalidated.
